title: How do I automate a repetitive task between two apps?
problem_statement: You keep copying information from one app to another by hand (form responses into a spreadsheet, attachments into a folder) and want it to happen automatically.
expected_outcome: A working automation that runs on its own and that you have tested with real data.

steps.title: Describe the task as a rule
steps.instructions: Write it as 'When X happens in app A, do Y in app B'. Note how often it happens each month.
steps.expected_result: A one-line rule and an estimate of monthly volume.

steps.title: Pick an automation tool
steps.instructions: For a simple two-app rule with low volume, a hosted tool with a free tier such as Zapier is the quickest start. If you are technical and want to self-host, n8n's Community edition is free to run on your own server.
steps.expected_result: A tool chosen with its limits understood.

steps.title: Connect both apps
steps.instructions: Sign in to app A and app B from the automation tool and grant only the permissions it needs.

steps.title: Build and test
steps.instructions: Set the trigger and the action, map the fields, then run a test with a real example.
steps.expected_result: The test item appears correctly in app B.

steps.title: Turn it on and monitor
steps.instructions: Switch the automation on and check it daily for the first week.
steps.expected_result: The automation runs reliably without your help.
steps.warning: Watch usage against plan limits so it doesn't stop unexpectedly.

quality_checks: A real event triggers the automation within the expected time.
Data lands in the right fields in app B.
You know what happens if the plan limit is reached.

editorial.author: V2 research pass (AI-assisted, Claude)
editorial.change_summary: Researched from official sources 2026-10-21; published under owner's blanket MVP approval (D-044). Domain-expert review pending.

budget_note: Zapier's free plan covers 100 tasks per month with two-step Zaps; n8n self-hosted Community edition is free but needs a server.
common_mistakes: Automating a process that isn't stable yet
Giving the tool more account access than needed
Not checking the monthly task limit
privacy_or_safety_notes: Automations copy data between services; avoid moving sensitive personal data unless you have checked both services' privacy terms.
